title: A Phase 1/2, Open-Label Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Efficacy of Intravenous ATR 1072 for the Treatment of PRKAG2 Syndrome
abstract: ATR 1072 is an investigational medicine being studied in adults with PRKAG2 Syndrome. This study will evaluate the safety of ATR 1072 and how the body processes the drug. Researchers will also assess how ATR 1072 affects PRKAG2 activity and measures of heart disease.
description: ATR 1072 is an antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) designed to reduce expression of PRKAG2 through targeted delivery of siRNA to cardiac tissue. This first-in-human, Phase 1/2, open-label, multicenter study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and exploratory efficacy of multiple doses of ATR 1072 in adults with PRKAG2 Syndrome. The study consists of a multiple ascending dose portion (Part A) followed by a dose-expansion cohort at the dose selected in (Part A). After completion of a 48-week treatment period, participants in Parts A and B enter a 42-week extension period followed by a post-treatment follow-up of up to 18 weeks. Approximately 37 participants will be enrolled globally.

title: Precision Phenotyping of Behavioral Risk and Response to Electromagnetic and Psychedelic Therapies
abstract: PRE-EMPT will assemble a cohort of 150 participants from three populations (low risk, intermediate risk, and high risk for self-harm). We will obtain clinical assessments, structural and functional MRI utilizing tasks pioneered by our team to assess cognitive control (CC) and emotion regulation (ER), and peripheral circular RNA (circRNA) levels to characterize the molecular brain states associated with behavioral risk. The clinical, imaging, and transcriptomic data will be fused and jointly analyzed to increase the accuracy of our risk prediction models. PRE-EMPT in three separate Aims will then prospectively assess three promising and innovative interventions for their potential to reduce suicidal ideation and alter activity in key neural networks: 1) neurofeedback (NF) using real-time fMRI with simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), 2) a form of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) called accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) with dose optimization through electric field modeling; and 3) psilocybin assisted therapy (PSI), with flexible dosing plan to maximize the depth of psychedelic experience. These therapies were chosen based on our team's prior work in all three interventions demonstrating rapid action and large effects.

title: A Phase 1/2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety of an Acne mRNA Vaccine Candidate in Adolescents 12 to 17 Years of Age With Moderate to Severe Acne
abstract:
The purpose of this study is to assess the safety profile of intramuscular injections of the Acne mRNA vaccine at 3 dose levels compared with placebo in 12 to 17 years old participants with moderate to severe acne.

An early safety data review (ESDR) will be conducted after each subcohort has completed an injection round; enrollment of the next higher dose level subcohort or progression of a subcohort to the subsequent injection round will only proceed if no safety concerns are identified. This sequential process will allow a cautious approach to vaccine injection in the adolescent population.

Study details are as follows:

* Before being enrolled in the study, participants complete a 4-week (ie, 1-month) screening period during which they will be called over the telephone approximately in the middle of the screening period to check they are not using prohibited medications and to remind them about the facial hygiene requirements.
* Once the screening period has been completed, the study duration will be up to 13 months for each participant
* Participants will be invited to a long-term extension study through a separate protocol.

title: MIA-COMP Pivotal Study: COMParative Self-Collection for Cervical Cancer Screening
abstract:
To evaluate whether individuals drawn from the intended use population can successfully interpret and follow the IFU for the Mia by XytoTest self-collection device and perform a vaginal sample collection yielding sufficient cellular material for primary hrHPV screening.

To assess the clinical performance of Mia self-collected vaginal specimens by evaluating agreement with paired clinician-collected cervical specimens for the detection of high-risk HPV, when both specimen types are analyzed using the cobas HPV Test (Roche Molecular Systems). Residual samples may be used to determine adequacy for additional assays that require vaginal and/or cervical specimens (such as mRNA E6 and E7 Biomarker Test, dual stain cytology).
description: The purpose of this pivotal study is to generate the clinical evidence necessary to support FDA marketing authorization for the Mia device. Specifically, the study will evaluate the diagnostic agreement of Mia-collected self-samples against the standard of care clinician-collected method for primary hrHPV detection, confirm device safety, demonstrate that end users across a diverse population can use the device safely and effectively as directed.

title: Phase 1/2 Base-Edited Hematopoietic Stem/Progenitor Cell Gene Therapy for Treatment of CXCR4-WHIM
abstract:
Background:

Warts, hypogammaglobulinemia, infections and myelokathexis syndrome (WHIMs) is a rare disorder that affects the immune system. People with WHIMs can have severe infections all over their body. WHIMs is caused by a mutation in the CXCR4 gene. Treatment with drugs can help control the infections but does not cure the disorder. Researchers want to try a treatment where they collect stem cells from a person with WHIMS, use base-editing to replace the bad gene with a healthy version, and return the new cells to the person. This could cure WHIMs.

Objective:

To test a treatment using base-edited stem cells in people with WHIMs.

Eligibility:

People aged 3 years and older with WHIMs.

Design:

The study has 4 stages.

Stage 1: Screening. Participants will be screened at 1 or more visits. They will have a physical exam with blood tests. A sample of tissue and fluid (biopsy) will be taken from the bone marrow in the hip.

Stage 2: Apheresis. Blood will be taken from the body through a needle; the blood will pass through a machine that separates out the stem cells. The remaining blood will be returned to the body through a different needle. The collected stem cells will undergo gene editing.

Stage 3: Treatment. Participants will stay in the hospital for about 4 weeks. They will receive 3 drugs to prepare their body for the procedure. Then the edited stem cells will be returned to their bloodstream. They will stay in the hospital until they recover.

Stage 4: Follow-up. Participants will have 8 follow-up visits over 5 years. Long-term visits will continue for 15 years.
description:
Study Description:

This is a phase 1/2, non-randomized study of a single infusion of autologous hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) base-edited to repair CXCR4 mutations in 10 participants with (Warts, Hypogammaglobulinemia, Infections, and Myelokathexis) WHIM syndrome.

Primary Objective: Evaluate safety of treatment with BE-HSPC CXCR4 in participants with WHIM syndrome.

Secondary Objectives:

Evaluate:

* Efficacy.
* Genetic correction.
* Immune reconstitution.
* Clinical efficacy.

Exploratory Objective:

Evaluate off-target (OT) editing activity.

Primary Endpoint:

Safety assessed by:

* Incidence of adverse events (AEs) for each participant.
* Evaluate overall incidence of AEs for the study.
* Incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs).

Secondary Endpoints (24 months post-study agent infusion):

* Efficacy: \>= 5% gene edited circulating myeloid cells by 12 months after BE HSPC infusion.
* Gene correction:

  --Frequency of corrected alleles in peripheral blood cells (such as myeloid, T, B, and natural killer \[NK\] cells).

  --\>200/microL edited neutrophils by 12 months post receipt of the BE HSPC infusion.
* Immune reconstitution:

  * T, B, and NK cell number improvement from baseline.
  * B-cell function: immunoglobulin (Ig) production.
* Clinical efficacy: Improvement from baseline problems such as recurrent infection, wart burden, gastrointestinal complaints, or immune dysregulation.

Exploratory Endpoint:

Evaluate for frequency of OTs by high-throughput sequencing (HTS) of the target mutation at the genomic locus 2 years post-infusion.

title: A PHASE 3 CLINICAL STUDY EVALUATING THE SAFETY, TOLERABILITY, AND IMMUNOGENICITY OF BNT162B2 RNA-BASED, VARIANT-ADAPTED VACCINE CANDIDATE(S) AGAINST SARS-COV-2 IN CHILDREN AND ADULTS
abstract:
The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety and effects of updated COVID-19 vaccines (called BNT162b2) in participants 5 Through 64 Years of Age with risk factors for Severe COVID-19, and Participants 65 Years of Age and Older.

This study is seeking participants who:

* are medically stable
* have not had a recent COVID-19 infection or a recent COVID-19 vaccination
* have not received certain routine vaccines recently
* participants that are 5 through 64 years of age will need to have at least 1 medical condition that increase their risk of complications from COVID-19.

Participants in Cohort 1 of this study will receive a single age-appropriate dose (30 mcg for participants aged ≥12 years; 10 mcg for participants aged 5-11 years) of BNT162b2 vaccine 1 which targets COVID-19 (2026/2027 recommended strain) injected in the upper arm. The study team and participants will know which injection they receive.

Participants in Cohort 2 of this study will randomly receive 1 injection into their upper arm of either: BNT162b2 vaccine 1; BNT162b2 vaccine 2, or BNT162b2 vaccine 3 which targets COVID-19. The study team and participants will not know which injection they receive.

Participants enrolled in Cohort 1 will be in the study for about 2 months and will have at least 3 scheduled visits. Participants enrolled in Cohort 2 will be in the study for about 6 months and will have at least 3 scheduled visits. Participants will record side effects and complete diaries following visit procedures. For Cohort 1 the study team will collect a nose swab and blood samples at 2 of the 3 visits. For Cohort 2 the study team will collect a nose swab and blood samples at all of the visits.

abstract: This study will evaluate 2 dose levels of mRNA-1283 in participants ≥6 months to \<12 years to determine the optimal dose level per age group.
description:
mRNA-1283 will be administered at 2 different dose levels (Dose Level 1 and Dose Level 2), with mRNA-1273 serving as the active comparator. Dose Level 1 will be the lower dose, and Dose Level 2 will be the higher dose.

The study will consist of 2 cohorts. In Cohort 1, mRNA-1283 will be administered as a single dose to participants aged ≥2 to \<12 years, regardless of prior coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination status, with mRNA-1273 included as a comparator. In Cohort 2, mRNA-1283 will be administered as a 2-dose series to participants aged ≥6 months to \<2 years who are previously unvaccinated for COVID-19, with mRNA-1273 included as a comparator.

title: Randomized, Double-blind, Phase II Trial of Vortosiran to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacodynamic Efficacy in Participants With Prior Venous Thromboembolism After Completion of Initial Anticoagulant Therapy (Cohort A) and in Cancer Patients at High Risk of Venous Thromboembolism (Cohort B)
abstract:
Blood clots remain a serious cause of illness and death. Long-term treatment and prevention of these clots with blood thinners is often limited by bleeding risk, drug interactions, and daily dosing, leading many patients to stop treatment early. Both cancer and chemotherapy further increase the risk of clot formation.

Vortosiran is an injectable therapy that lowers Factor XI (one of the body's natural clotting helpers) production in the liver, leading to a strong and long-lasting reduction in blood clotting activity with less risk of bleeding compared to current available treatments. Studies conducted so far have shown that vortosiran is safe and shows a dose-dependent Factor XI suppression (that is, a higher dose results in a higher level of suppression) that lasts for several months, supporting testing using a limited number of injections in patients who are at higher risk of blod clot formation.

This study aims to study how safe and effective vortosiran is in patients who have had blood clots in the past and in cancer patients who are at high risk of developing blood clots.
description:
Venous thromboembolism, encompassing DVT and PE, is a common condition with a durable risk of recurrence after completion of initial therapy with systemic anticoagulation. In a systematic review and meta-analysis of patients with a first unprovoked VTE who completed at least 3 months of anticoagulant therapy and then discontinued treatment, the cumulative incidence of recurrent VTE was approximately 10% in the first year, 25% at 5 years, and 36% at 10 years, with recurrent events carrying measurable case fatality (Khan et al, 2019). Decisions about extended therapy are frequently individualized because continued anticoagulation reduces VTE recurrence but also exposes patients to ongoing bleeding risk, treatment burden, and complexity of care.

Venous thromboembolism, including in patients with cancer and chemotherapy, remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Despite effective anticoagulants, long-term management is constrained by clinically meaningful bleeding risk, drug-drug interactions with anticoagulation therapy, and the need for continuous dosing and adherence. Furthermore, many patients discontinue therapy when they perceive recurrence risk to be moderate or when bleeding risk, treatment burden, or patient preference argues against indefinite anticoagulation. These combined factors constitute an unmet need for a convenient strategy that can reduce recurrent VTE risk with a lower risk of bleeding.

Vortosiran is a subcutaneously administered siRNA designed to selectively inhibit hepatic synthesis of FXI, resulting in robust and durable suppression of FXI activity. FXI inhibition is novel and innovative anti-thrombotic strategy inhibiting blood clot formation by the intrinsic pathway without interfering with hemostatic control through the extrinsic and commen clotting pathways. Thereby reducing blood clot formation and VTE without increasing the risk of bleeding compared to current available anti-coagulant treatments.

This Phase II trial is designed to establish dose-related FXI suppression, characterize safety with repeated dosing, and generate an initial signal on clinical outcomes in two VTE prevention settings.

This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase II trial will be conducted in two cohorts. Cohort A and Cohort B are independently enrolled and randomized. Participants are randomized (2:2:1) to low-dose vortosiran, high-dose vortosiran, or matched placebo, with dosing on Day X and Day Y and follow-up through Week 56. This trial aims to evaluate vortosiran in two complementary populations where FXI suppression could provide clinically relevant benefit and where the risk-benefit of conventional anticoagulation is often challenging.

* Cohort A (post-VTE, with participants judged to be at equipoise for extended therapy): Participants have completed 3 to 12 months of standard anticoagulation for symptomatic proximal DVT and/or PE as originally prescribed, and have had no recurrence during that initial treatment period. The cohort is restricted to patients for whom discontinuation of anticoagulation is consistent with local standard of care and where there is true equipoise about extended therapy vs only follow-up and observation.
* Cohort B (active cancer; high VTE risk): Ambulatory patients initiating a new course of systemic chemotherapy and with intermediate to high VTE risk (Khorana score ≥2), but no history of prior VTE.

title: A Phase 4 Open-label, Single-arm Study to Evaluate the Safety and Immunogenicity of an Omicron Subvariant-based SARS-CoV-2 Recombinant Spike (rS) Vaccine Adjuvanted With Matrix-M in Participants ≥ 65 Years of Age and Participants 12 Through 64 Years of Age Who Are at Increased Risk for Severe COVID-19 Illness
abstract:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a single dose of Sanofi's Omicron subvariant-based Nuvaxovid in participants ≥ 65 years of age and participants 12 through 64 years of age who have at least one underlying condition that puts them at increased risk for severe outcomes of COVID-19 and who have been previously vaccinated with a COVID-19 vaccine ≥ 90 days prior to study vaccination.

Study details include:

* The study duration will be approximately 3 months per participant.
* Study intervention will be administered via a single intramuscular (IM) injection into the deltoid muscle on Day 1.
* The visit frequency will be Day 1, Day 9 telephone call, Day 29, and Day 91 telephone call (3-month safety follow-up).

title: A Phase 1b Study of Tocilizumab Combined With Chemo-Immunotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients With Cancer-Associated Weight Loss and Elevated Inflammatory Markers. The TOCI Study
abstract: This is a Phase 1b/2, multi-site, single-arm, open-label, non-randomized study looking at whether adding tocilizumab to standard treatment for metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) is safe, possible, and effective. The study includes people with metastatic NSCLC, that is lung cancer that has spread, who have experienced significant loss of weight or muscle mass.
description:
Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for approximately 85% of all diagnoses. For patients with metastatic NSCLC lacking actionable driver mutations (e.g., EGFR, ALK), the standard first-line therapeutic strategy involves immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) axis, administered either as monotherapy or in combination with platinum-doublet chemotherapy. While these regimens have significantly improved overall survival (OS), a substantial proportion of patients fail to derive durable clinical benefit, and long-term survival rates for metastatic disease remain suboptimal, often due to host-related factors that impair the anti-tumor immune response.

A critical determinant of poor therapeutic outcomes in advanced NSCLC is cancer-associated cachexia (CAC), a multifactorial paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by systemic inflammation, negative protein-energy balance, and the involuntary loss of skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia). Primary observational studies demonstrate that nutritional derangements closely associated with cachexia - such as significant weight loss and malnutrition - are highly prevalent in lung cancer, particularly in advanced disease, with lung cancer-specific cohorts reporting rates ranging from approximately 35% - 70% depending on disease stage and assessment method. Unlike starvation, it is driven by aberrant systemic inflammation and not fully reversible via nutritional support.

Clinically, cachexia is defined by the international consensus (Fearon criteria) as weight loss \>5% over 6 months, or weight loss \>2% in individuals with a body mass index (BMI) \< 20 kilograms per square meter (kg/m2) or sarcopenia. Sarcopenia is specifically defined by a low skeletal muscle index (SMI) at the L3 vertebral level, with widely validated cutoffs of \< 52.4 cm2/m2 for men and \< 8.5 cm2/m2 for women.

This is a Phase 1b/2, multi-site, single-arm, open-label, non-randomized study looking at whether adding tocilizumab to standard treatment for metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) is safe, possible, and effective. The study includes people with metastatic NSCLC, that is lung cancer that has spread, who have experienced significant loss of weight or muscle mass.

Primary Objective Evaluate the safety/feasibility and efficacy of adding tocilizumab to standard first-line chemo-immunotherapy in biomarker-selected patients with stage IV NSCLC, defined by weight loss ≥5% within the prior 6 months, or ≥2% if BMI \< 20 kilograms per square meter (kg/m2).

Co-primary endpoint 1: Safety/Feasibility Proportion of patients completing four cycles of chemo-IO + tocilizumab without grade ≥3 autoimmune or non-hematological treatment-related adverse events (TRAE). Feasibility will be defined as ≥80% completion; unacceptable toxicity as \>30% incidence of grade ≥3 serious AEs.

Co-primary endpoint 2: Progression-Free Survival Rate at 6 months Proportion of patients alive and progression-free at 6 months after starting therapy per RECIST v1.1, estimated by Kaplan-Meier and presented with a 95% CI.

Secondary Objectives Assess the effect of tocilizumab on body composition, inflammatory biomarkers, and treatment response.

Secondary Endpoints: change in weight/muscle mass (CT-based sarcopenia/Fearon index); Overall Response Rate (ORR); median Overall Survival Rate; and CRP levels from baseline to end of treatment.

Correlative Objectives Evaluate associations between treatment response (PFS rate at 6 months, ORR) and baseline inflammatory biomarkers (CRP) as well as molecular biomarkers (KRAS, STK11) identified by next-generation sequencing (NGS) of tumor tissue.

Exploratory Objectives Identify associations between treatment response (PFS rate at 6 months, ORR) and longitudinal measurements of CRP, IL-6, Cyclin D1 and Bcl-xL mRNA, as well as baseline PTPRT methylation.

Participants will go through the screening and baseline process to assess eligibility. If eligible, participants will attend study treatment visits every 21 days for about 3 months, an End of Treatment (EOT) visit about 30 days after the last dose of treatment, and follow up for up to 12 months after the EOT visit. Tocilizumab will be administered in addition to standard treatment regimens for NSCLC, at a dose of 8 mg/kg intravenous (IV) once every three weeks (once every 21 days); on day one of each treatment cycle. Tocilizumab is administered as a single IV drip infusion over 1 hour; it cannot be administered as bolus or push. Tocilizumab will be given for 4 doses, at the beginning of treatment, or until disease progression or unacceptable toxicities.

The study will be open at 4 VA hospitals, and planned enrollment is about 43 participants in total with about 11 participants from each site. This research study is expected to take about 4 years. Individual participation in the study will take about 18 months.

title: Study on the Mechanism of Central Obesity Induced by Sleep Restriction and the Therapeutic Effect of n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid: a Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Trial (COSPA Study)
abstract:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to investigate whether n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation attenuates abdominal visceral fat accumulation induced by experimental sleep restriction.

Forty healthy adults aged 18-50 years will be randomly assigned to receive n-3 PUFA supplementation (approximately 1.1 g/day of EPA and DHA) or a matching placebo. The intervention will last approximately 75 days, including a 19-day residential sleep protocol consisting of 3 adaptation days, 14 days of sleep restriction (4 hours per night), and 2 recovery days.

The primary outcome is the change in abdominal visceral adipose tissue area measured by CT. Additional assessments include body composition, metabolic and inflammatory markers, gut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and adipose tissue molecular profiles.
description:
Experimental sleep restriction provides a controlled model for investigating the metabolic consequences of insufficient sleep. This study will examine whether n-3 PUFA supplementation modifies visceral fat accumulation and related biological responses during sleep restriction.

Participants will undergo a standardized residential sleep protocol with continuous polysomnographic monitoring. Abdominal CT will be performed on Days 3 and 17 to assess changes in visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue. Additional measurements will include dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, cognitive assessments, biological sample collection, and exploratory molecular analyses.

The study will also explore potential mechanisms involving gut microbiota, microbial metabolism, inflammation, and adipose tissue responses.

outcomes.measure: Change in Visceral Adipose Tissue Area
outcomes.description: Change in abdominal visceral adipose tissue area measured by CT, calculated as the value on Day 17 minus the value on Day 3, expressed in cm².

outcomes.measure: Change in Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue Area
outcomes.description: Change in abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) area measured by CT, calculated as SAT area on Day 17 minus SAT area on Day 3 (ΔSAT), expressed in cm²

outcomes.measure: Change in Total Abdominal Adipose Tissue Area
outcomes.description: Change in total abdominal adipose tissue (TAT) area measured by CT, calculated as TAT area on Day 17 minus TAT area on Day 3 (ΔTAT), expressed in cm²

outcomes.measure: Change in Visceral-to-Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue Ratio
outcomes.description: Change in the ratio of visceral to subcutaneous adipose tissue area (VAT/SAT), calculated as the ratio on Day 17 minus the ratio on Day 3

outcomes.measure: Changes in Gut Microbial Alpha Diversity (Shannon Index)
outcomes.description: Changes in fecal gut microbial alpha diversity measured by the Shannon diversity index using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Shannon index values reflect microbial richness and evenness and are unitless.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks before the residential phase (T0), Day 3 (T1), Day 10, and Day 17 (T2)

outcomes.measure: Changes in Gut Microbial Beta Diversity (Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity)
outcomes.description: Changes in gut microbial community composition assessed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing data. Between-sample differences will be evaluated using PERMANOVA.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks before the residential phase (T0), Day 3 (T1), Day 10, and Day 17 (T2)

outcomes.description: Changes in the relative abundance of gut microbial taxa assessed by fecal microbiome sequencing and differential abundance analysis

outcomes.measure: Changes in Fecal Short-Chain Fatty Acid Concentrations
outcomes.description: Changes in fecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations, including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, assessed using metabolomic methods.

title: Impact of Significant Surgical Reduction of Adipose Tissue on Plasma Levels and Genetic Expression of Adipokines Associated With Ischemic Heart Disease in Type I Obesity.
abstract:
Adipose tissue is with endocrine properties and secretes many cytokines. Some of these cytokines are concerned with ischemic heart disease. I hypothesized that significant surgical reduction in adipose tissue mass leads to decrease in its cell population which may pose significantly reduced production of adipokines ( Leptin and Angiotensin) associated with ischemic heart disease in obese people.

Study objectives are analysis of Leptin, Angiotensin-II, mRNA expression analysis of leptin, leptin receptor and Angiotensin-II. investigation of genetic variations in the Leptin, Leptin receptors, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors, confirm SNPs of selected sample. Ddetermination of the association of genetic variation in Leptin receptor, angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors with Leptin and Angiotensin-II levels and determination of effect of genetic variation on the transcriptional regulation.

Case control study having 212 patients (106 patients in each group) with type I Obese adults, both males and pre-menopausal females belonging to ASA 1 and 2 requiring stagged liposuction will be included. Exclusion of subjects with Diabetes mellitus, Metabolic syndrome, Endocrine disorders, on statin drugs, not willing to participate.

After informed consent, blood samples will be taken to quantify plasma levels of Leptin and Angiotensin II pre-operatively by ELISA.

DNA will also be extracted from blood and SNPs will be analysed. The selected SNPs will be amplified by PCR and product will be purified and analysed by agarose gel electrophoresis.

Patients will undergo liposuction and RNA will be isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue for reverse transcription.

After 3 months, patients will be called back for second session of liposuction and plasma level of Leptin and Angiotensin II will be quantified again. Similarly, expression profile of transcription factors will also be analysed again. Paired t-test will be used to compare clinical parameters like serum adipokines levels and adipokines expression levels and p value \<0.05 will be taken as statistically significant. The results will be utilized to determine impact of surgical reduction on plasma level and expression of the adipokines in minimizing cardiovascular risk factors.
description:
INTRODUCTION:

Overweight and obesity belong to the main public healthcare problems in many developed countries. Causes of obesity are considered to be the combination of genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors. In case of morbid obesity, the human organism suffers from an excess of subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue.1 Adipose tissue plays a principal role in overall metabolic homeostasis, and its dysfunction can lead to metabolic disorders, most notably type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.2 Mature adipocytes express all components of the renin- angiotensin system (RAS) including angiotensin Il (Ang II), and also express the type 1 (AT1) and type 2 (AT 2) angiotensin receptor subtypes.3 For cardiovascular disease, perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) is a specific adipose tissue and now recognized to be an endocrine organ with important physiological and pathological effects on vascular homeostasis and vascular diseases.(4) PVAT dysfunction may induce several pathophysiological states such as obesity, atherosclerosis or hypertension.4-6 There are essentially two major types of adipose tissue with different functions: brown adipose tissue (BAT) containing multiple lipid droplets and densely packed mitochondria, and white adipose tissue (WAT) with large lipid droplets and relatively low expression levels of UCP-1(mitochondrial uncoupling protein-1).4 Ang II is produced from angiotensin I (Ang I as a result of the catalytic action of angiotensin-converting enzyme I (ACE-1). Ang Il plays an important role in the regulation of blood volume, blood pressure, cardiac function, and electrolyte balance.7 On the other hand, Leptin is a protein classified within the adipokine family and is currently recognized as a hormone consisting of 167 amino acids with a molecular weight of 16 kD. It is predominantly synthesized in adipocytes, and its production is contingent upon the volume of fat deposits in the body. It is known that leptin inhibits the orexigenic pathway and stimulates the anorexigenic pathway, underscoring its pivotal role in body weight regulation.8 The relationship between leptin and the RAAS is bi-directional. Leptin not only stimulates sympathetic nervous system activation and angiotensin-dependent mechanisms, but it also seems to be a major driver in the aldosterone production in obese patients.9 Moreover, leptin appears to play a role in heart protection. The increased blood volume in obese patients increases cardiac output and stimulates biomechanical stress and structural remodeling that may result in cardiac hypertrophy. A correlation between plasma leptin levels and cardiac hypertrophy has been clinically demonstrated.10 There is evidence for both angiotensin and leptin receptors in several brain regions involved in regulation of sympathetic nerve activity. Ang II may modulate the action of leptin and adiponectin in obesity. Blocking of RAS increases plasma adiponectin suggesting a role of Ang II in decreased levels of adiponectin. Supporting this, Ang I1 infusion decreased plasma adiponectin and adiponectin mRNA in adipose tissue. Ang II also interacts with adiponectin in their target cells.11 Considering the role of Ang II and Leptin in the regulation of obesity, I hypothesized that significant surgical reduction in adipose tissue mass leads to decrease in its cell population which may pose significantly reduced production of adipokines associated with ischemic heart disease in obese people.

OBJECTIVES:

Analysis of adipokine levels (Leptin, Angiotensin-II) in patients with type I obesity (Quazi Experimental).

mRNA expression analysis of leptin, leptin receptor and Angiotensin-II (Quazi Experimental).

Investigation of genetic variations in the Leptin, Leptin receptors, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors (Case Control).

Confirm SNPs of selected sample. Determine the association of genetic variation in Leptin receptor, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors with Leptin and Angiotensin-II levels.

Determine effect of genetic variation on the transcriptional regulation.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION:

Significant Fat Reduction A removal of 1 liter or more lipoaspirate through liposuction will be considered as significant.

Tumescence Injection of fluid in the fat removal area containing Ringer Lactate each litter with 40ml 2% xylocaine and 1ml of 1:1000 Epinephrine till the area is blanched and showing fountain sign.

Polymorphism Defined a discontinuous genetic variation resulting in the occurrence of several different forms or types of individuals among the members of a single species. A discontinuous genetic variation divides the individuals of a population into two or more sharply distinct forms.

HYPOTHESIS:

Significant surgical reduction of adipose tissue reduces the level of adipokines (Leptin and Angiotensin) associated with cardiac risk in plasma and their expression in adipose tissue.

MATERIAL AND METHODS:

Study design Case control study. Setting The study will be conducted at Advanced Research Centre for Biomedical Sciences (ARCBS), KEMU and Jinnah Burn and Reconstructive Surgery Center / AIMC, Lahore.

Duration The study will be expected to complete within two years after the approval of synopsis.

Sample size Sample size of 212 patients (106 patients in each group) is estimated by using 95% confidence level and 10% absolute precision with expected percentage LEPrs7799039 as in FEN as 19.1% and healthy control as 14.1%.(12) n = Z 1-α/2 \[P1 (1- P1) +P2 (1- P2)\] d2 Z 1-α/2 = confidence level 95 % = 1.96 P1 = population proportion I = 19.1% P2 = population proportion II = 14% d2 = absolute precision 10% SNP analysis will be done in all the 212 subjects with 106 taken as cases (Obese type 1) and 106 as controls (Normal BMI).

Out of 106 cases, liposuction will be performed in selected subjects. Similarly, sequencing will be done in selected subjects. Sampling technique Non Probability Consecutive Sampling.

SAMPLE SELECTION:

Inclusion Criteria: Type I Obese adults, both males and pre-menopausal females, Patients requiring stagged liposuction, American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) class 1 and 2 (as determined by consultant anesthesiologist) Exclusion Criteria: Patients who are with Diabetes mellitus, Metabolic syndrome, Endocrine disorders, on statin drugs, not willing to participate.

DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE:

Informed consent will be obtained from the study subjects for donation of blood and adipose tissue samples in the proposed study, which will be conducted under a protocol approved by the Institutional Review Board of King Edward Medical University (Appendix I). The information of the study subjects will be kept confidential, and the subjects will be recruited against lab record number or archive number.

Sample Collection: Patients will undergo lipo-aspiration under tumescence by Colman's technique. Each unit of tumescent fluid will include xylocaine 40ml, Hartmann's solution 1000ml and 1ml adrenaline. A multi hole 5mm liposuction cannula attached with suction machine will be inserted through the incisions using controlled back and forth motion. All the patients will be followed fortnightly. Analysis of pre and post procedure blood and adipose tissue samples will be done. For DNA extraction, 5ml blood will be collected.

Quantification of Serum Adipokines levels by ELISA: Serum will be separated after clotting through centrifugation at 3000 rpm and stored at -70°C. ELIS A will be performed on samples by standard protocol for the quantification of adipokines (Leptin, Angiotensin I1) pre-operatively and three months post operatively DNA Extraction: 5ml blood will be collected in EDTA-coated tubes. Genomic DNA will be extracted from whole blood by using commercially available kits.

Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism Analysis of SNPs: The selected SNPs will be amplified by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) by using the primers given in Table 1. Amplicons will be detected on 2.5% agarose gel and stained with DNA gel stain. DNA bands will be detected by gel documentation instrument under UV light. PCR product will be purified by using commercially available kit and digested with restriction enzymes. The restriction product will be analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis.

Sequencing of SNPs: Sequencing of SNPs will be done using specific primers by Sanger Sequence using ABI 3500, Genetic Analyzer (Applied Biosystems, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) and the sequences will be analyzed using the BLAST program at National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). Amino acid sequences will be predicted by the standard code and will be aligned using the ExPASY online tool for translation. Sequencing will be done on study subjects and compared with same number of healthy persons for comparison.

RNA Isolation and cDNA Synthesis: RNA will be isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue by using commercially available kits. 1ug RNA will be reverse transcribed using commercially available Transcription First Strand cDNA kit and oligo (dT) primers.

Real-time PCR Analysis for Gene Expression Analysis: Quantitative real-time PCR analysis will be carried out by using SYBR Green real-time PCR Master Mix and an ARIAmix, real-time PCR system (Agilent Technologies). Cycling conditions for real-time PCR will be 3 min at 95°C, followed by 40 cycles of 30 S at 95°C, 30 S at 60°C and 30 S at 72°C. Results will be analysed using the ΔΔCt method and will be presented as fold difference in mRNA level relative to GAPDH. The expression profile of transcription factors will be analyzed.

DATA ANALYSIS PRODECURE:

Data will be entered and analyzed using statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS-26). Quantitative variables like age, BMI, lipid profile and adipokine levels will be presented as mean ± SD. Qualitative variables like family history of obesity, family history of heart diseases and gender will be presented frequency and percentages. Paired t-test will be used to compare clinical parameters like serum adipokines levels and adipokines expression levels. Odds ratio and 95% CI will be used for SNP analysis. Whereas p value \<0.05 will be taken as statistically significant. Pearson equation will be used to determine association of adipokines levels with clinical parameters and expression levels.

OUTCOME \& UTILIZATION:

The results will be utilized to determine impact of surgical reduction on plasma level and expression of the adipokines in minimizing cardiovascular risk factors.

title: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Single-Dose Phase 1 Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamic Profile of RG002C0106 Injection in Healthy Participants
abstract:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if RG002C0106 is safe in healthy participants . It will also learn about how the drug is absorbed, distributed， metablized and excrited. The main questions it aims to answer are:

What medical problems do participants have when taking RG002C0106? Researchers will compare RG002C0106 to a placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if RG002C0106 is safe to participants.

Participants will:

Take RG00C2C0106 or a placebo once. Visit the clinic once every 2 weeks/1 month for checkups and tests.
description:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-dose, phase I study in healthy adult participants.

A Safety Review Committee (SRC), composed of the sponsor, the Investigator and the sponsor representatives, will be established prior to study initiation.

Escalation to the next higher dose level will only be permitted if the SRC confirms an acceptable safety and tolerability profile based on safety data and available PK/PD assessments collected.

title: Study of Satellite Cells in COPD-associated sarcOPenia (Satellite Cells in COPD Sarcopenia) : Exploratory Cohort Study for Translational Research
abstract: The aim of the study is to decipher the alterations in signalling pathways of skeletal muscle stem cells (satellite cells (SCs)) in individuals with COPD, as well as to examine the effect of exercise training on SCs. To this end, the team will perform an exhaustive evaluation of lung and muscle function, including exercise capacity, as well as muscle biopsies, before and after a 2-months rehabilitation program. This study should provide new therapeutic avenues for COPD-associated sarcopenia.
description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is now to be considered as a multimorbid disease, originating from a combination of several risk factors (respiratory events in childhood, exposure to inhaled particles, physical inactivity, etc.), and simultaneously affecting several organs. This multi-organ impairment is likely to arise from common biological processes such as systemic inflammation or repair failure. Studying these processes in an organ that is easily accessible to biopsy, such as skeletal muscle, can help in the overall management of COPD. Skeletal muscle wasting (or sarcopenia: loss of muscle mass and force) is also a major comorbidity in COPD, both frequent and associated to increased mortality. Muscle stem cells (satellite cells) are responsible for repairing skeletal muscle tissue after injury, notably after micro-lesions induced by exercise. However, they have been scarcely studied in COPD. In the present project, the team proposes to study repair abnormalities in skeletal muscle tissue by comparing the signalling pathways activated in satellite cells of patients with COPD, before and after a respiratory rehabilitation programme (20 sessions over 8 to 12 weeks). The team will carry out an exhaustive respiratory and muscular assessment at inclusion and at the end of the 20 sessions, evaluating in particular respiratory function and exercise capacity (Pulmonary Function Tests, cardio-pulmonary exercise testing with VO2max measurement, 6-minute walking test, handgrip test) as well as a quadricipital muscle biopsy with the modified Bergström's technique. Muscle biopsies will be used to culture satellite cells and assess their regenerative capacity in vitro, as well as to analyse dysregulated signalling pathways at the transcriptomic level with single-cell RNAsequencing. The results should help to identify new therapeutic avenues for the comprehensive management of multimorbid COPD.

title: Effects of Non-invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation on Clinical, Peripheral Biologic, and Brain Measures of Stress Reactivity in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: a Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic disorder of gut-brain interaction that causes abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. Many people with IBS also experience symptoms outside the bowel, such as headaches, widespread pain, poor sleep, anxiety, and depression; these symptoms are especially common in females. This study focuses on stress reactivity (SR), a persistent pattern of stress-system activity that may be linked to autonomic nervous system function, immune activity, the gut microbiome, and brain processing. The investigators will enroll adults with at least moderate IBS symptoms and randomly assign them to 8 weeks of non-invasive vagal nerve stimulation (nVNS) or Usual Care. Participants assigned to nVNS will use a handheld device on the left side of the neck at home twice daily. The investigators will compare changes in IBS severity and other physical symptoms and examine whether baseline or treatment-related changes in blood, stool, heart-rate variability, sex hormones, and brain imaging measures are associated with response. The study will also explore whether treatment effects and predictors differ by sex.

outcomes.measure: Change in IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS)
outcomes.description: The IBS-SSS questionnaire is a validated measure of IBS symptom severity and has been shown to be responsive to treatment. The IBS-SSS assesses the severity of abdominal pain, frequency of abdominal pain, severity of abdominal distention, dissatisfaction with bowel habits, and interference of IBS with daily life over a 10-day period. Each of the five categories will receive a score from 0-100, and the total IBSSSS is calculated by taking the sum of these categories (range 0-500, 0 - no symptoms, 500 - very severe symptoms).
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Change in Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15)
outcomes.description: The PHQ-15 is a widely used measure of widespread somatic symptoms over 1 month that is sensitive to treatment effects. The PHQ-15 assess 15 different somatic symptoms (back pain, stomach pain, headaches, chest pain, trouble sleeping, etc.) rated by 0 - not bothered at all to 3 - bothered a lot. The scale is scored as follows: 0-4: Minimal somatic symptom severity, 5-9: Low somatic symptom severity, 10-14: Medium somatic symptom severity, 15-30: High somatic symptom severity.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Change in stress reactivity (SR)-related brain phenotypes.
outcomes.description: SR-related brain phenotypes will be derived from prespecified MRI measures of brain structure, functional connectivity, and brain activity. MRI data will be collected at baseline and Week 8. The primary imaging analysis will compare baseline-to-Week-8 change in prespecified SR-related brain phenotypes between nVNS and Usual Care.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: IBS Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS) responder rate
outcomes.description: The proportion of participants with IBS who experience a ≥50-point reduction in IBS-SSS score from baseline will be compared between treatment groups. A reduction of at least 50 points represents a clinically meaningful improvement in IBS symptoms. The IBS-SSS questionnaire is a validated measure of IBS symptom severity and has been shown to be responsive to treatment. The IBS-SSS assesses the severity of abdominal pain, frequency of abdominal pain, severity of abdominal distention, dissatisfaction with bowel habits, and interference of IBS with daily life over a 10-day period. Each of the five categories will receive a score from 0-100, and the total IBSSSS is calculated by taking the sum of these categories (range 0-500, 0 - no symptoms, 500 - very severe symptoms).
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Biologic measures of Stress Reactivity - SNS-Immune gene expression profile
outcomes.description: Changes in the sympathetic nervous system (SNS)-immune gene expression profile will be evaluated as a peripheral biologic measure of stress reactivity. Whole-blood SNS-immune gene expression will be measured using mRNA-targeted sequencing. Total RNA will be isolated from whole blood, converted to cDNA using Lexogen QuantSeq 3' FWD, sequenced using Illumina sequencing, mapped to the GRCh38 reference human transcriptome using STAR, and quantified as gene-specific reads per million mapped reads. Baseline-to-Week-8 changes will be compared between nVNS and Usual Care and examined in relation to clinical symptom change. Moderator analyses will also test whether baseline SNS-immune gene expression modifies the treatment response using an SNS-immune measure-by-treatment-by-time interaction.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Biologic measures of Stress Reactivity - heart rate variability (HRV)
outcomes.description: HRV will be evaluated as a peripheral autonomic measure of stress reactivity and compared over the treatment period. HRV will be derived from physiologic data collected using a Fitbit equipped with photoplethysmography sensors that estimate heart rate and intervals between successive beats. Participants will wear the device from baseline through the post-intervention assessment, including during sleep, to characterize longitudinal and circadian HRV. Changes in HRV will be compared between nVNS and Usual Care and correlated with symptom change. Moderator analyses will additionally test whether baseline HRV modifies treatment response through an HRV-by-treatment-by-time interaction.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Biologic measures of Stress Reactivity - fecal microbial stress index
outcomes.description: Changes in the fecal microbial stress index will be evaluated as a peripheral biologic measure of stress reactivity. The fecal microbial stress index will be derived from stool samples collected at baseline and Week 8 using shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Microbial sequencing data will undergo species-level taxonomic and functional characterization. Baseline-to-Week-8 changes in the microbial stress index will be compared between nVNS and Usual Care and correlated with clinical symptom change.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Biologic measures of Stress Reactivity - fecal metabolite stress index
outcomes.description: Changes in the fecal metabolite stress index will be evaluated as a peripheral biologic measure of stress reactivity. The fecal metabolite stress index will be derived from stool metabolomic data obtained using LC-MS/MS-based profiling. Baseline-to-Week-8 changes in the metabolite stress index will be compared between nVNS and Usual Care and correlated with clinical symptom change. Moderator analyses will additionally test whether the baseline metabolite stress index modifies treatment response through a metabolite stress index-by-treatment-by-time interaction.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Brain changes associated with IBS severity, comorbid symptom scores, and peripheral biologic measures of SR
outcomes.description: Examine associations between changes in scores on the SR-related brain phenotype signatures and changes in IBS severity, comorbid symptom scores, and peripheral biologic measures of SR. General linear models will examine associations between baseline-to-Week-8 changes in SR-related brain phenotype signature scores and corresponding changes in IBS-SSS, PHQ-15, HRV, SNS-immune gene expression, and microbial and metabolite stress indices, with adjustment for relevant covariates. Alternative approaches may be used to examine multivariate associations between changes in symptom severity, stress reactivity, comorbidity, and brain connectivity.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Change in extraintestinal symptoms in nVNS compared to Usual Care
outcomes.description: Predict response (Pre-Post change in extraintestinal symptoms) in nVNS compared to Usual Care. General linear model-based moderator analyses will evaluate whether baseline SR-related brain phenotype scores predict pre- to post-treatment change in extraintestinal symptom severity differently in participants assigned to nVNS versus Usual Care. Models will include baseline SR brain phenotype score, treatment group, the brain phenotype-by-treatment interaction, and prespecified covariates. A significant interaction will indicate differential prediction of treatment response.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

outcomes.measure: Exploratory outcome - Sex differences
outcomes.description: Examine whether females with IBS with higher comorbid symptom scores will present with greater changes in SR-related brain signatures following the nVNS intervention compared to male IBS. Exploratory models will examine whether females with IBS with greater baseline comorbid symptom burden demonstrate greater baseline-to-Week-8 changes in SR-related brain signatures following nVNS compared with males with IBS. The moderator analysis includes the comorbid symptom score-by-group interaction, with adjustment for age, BMI, and diet.
outcomes.time_frame: 8 weeks, from baseline to end of intervention

title: Treatment of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Paclitaxel Carried in Lipid Nanoparticles (LDE): a Randomized, Double-Blind Pilot Study of Safety and Feasibility
abstract: This pilot study evaluates the safety and feasibility of paclitaxel carried in cholesterol-rich lipid nanoparticles (LDE-paclitaxel) in heart transplant recipients with cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV). Changes in coronary atherosclerosis measured by intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) are assessed as secondary outcomes.
description:
Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a leading cause of late graft failure and death after heart transplantation and has no effective pharmacological treatment. LDE is a cholesterol-rich lipid nanoemulsion that binds to LDL receptors and concentrates in tissues with high receptor expression. In a rabbit heterotopic heart transplant model, LDE-paclitaxel reduced coronary stenosis and macrophage infiltration of the graft without observable toxicity. LDE-paclitaxel (175 mg/m²) was previously well tolerated in patients with breast and ovarian cancer and in patients with aortic atherosclerosis.

In this single-center, randomized (1:1), quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study, adult heart transplant recipients more than 1 year after transplantation with angiographically documented CAV receive six intravenous infusions, every 3 weeks, of LDE-paclitaxel (paclitaxel 175 mg/m² body surface area) or LDE without paclitaxel (placebo), each infused over 2 hours without premedication. Coronary angiography and IVUS of up to three epicardial vessels are performed at baseline and approximately 1 month after the sixth infusion, and IVUS analyses are performed in matched segments by an analyst blinded to treatment allocation. Laboratory safety tests are performed before each infusion, and participants are followed clinically for 12 months after the follow-up angiography.

The protocol planned 24 participants (20 plus 20% anticipated losses); 22 were enrolled.

title: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of ALN-CIDEB in Adults With Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease (ALD) With Moderate to Advanced Fibrosis
abstract:
This study will test a Regeneron study drug called ALN-CIDEB to find out whether it may help treat a liver disease called alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). ALD is a type of liver disease caused by drinking alcohol at levels that are harmful to the body. The study will also test ALN-CIDEB in participants who are known to have metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol- associated liver disease (MetALD), a subgroup of people that have features of both ALD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

The study will compare 2 different dose regimens of ALN-CIDEB with placebo (something that looks like the study drug but doesn't contain any medicine) to understand how well ALN-CIDEB works to lower the amount of fat in the liver.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects ALN-CIDEB might cause
* How well ALN-CIDEB works to change liver fat and stiffness of the liver
* How ALN-CIDEB could affect the liver proteins

title: A Double-blind, Randomized, Controlled, Multiple Ascending Dose Study of Intrathecally Administered CMP-002 in Participants With SYNGAP1-Related Disorder
abstract: The primary purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of CMP-002 in participants with SYNGAP1-related disorder.
description: ASCEND is a global, Phase 1/2, multicenter, randomized, double-blind (Sponsor-open), controlled, multiple-ascending dose (MAD) study to assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics, of CMP-002 in participants with SYNGAP1-related disorder (SRD). The study consists of a Baseline Period in which participants will undergo screening assessments to establish the baseline for clinical study assessments. The Baseline Period is followed by a Treatment Period consisting of 3 planned dose level cohorts wherein each participant will receive 3 doses of CMP-002 administered intrathecally (IT) or a control procedure on Days 1, 29, and 85. Each dose level cohort includes a minimum of 8 participants randomized in a 3:1 ratio (CMP-002: control). Following the completion of Dose 3, participants will be followed for an additional 24 weeks in the Follow-up Period.

title: A Single-Center, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Dose Escalation Phase I Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Subcutaneous Administration of JAR-2203 in Healthy Participants
abstract: This first-in-human Phase 1 study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and effects on Lp(a) of single ascending doses of JAR-2203 in healthy adults with elevated Lp(a).
description: JAR-2203 is an investigational small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting LPA mRNA to reduce plasma lipoprotein(a) \[Lp(a)\] levels. This first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of JAR-2203 in healthy participants with elevated Lp(a). Approximately 44 participants will be enrolled across six sequential dose cohorts, with dose escalation based on review by a Safety Review Committee.

title: Impact of Synbiotic Supplementation on Lipogenic and Adipogenic Factors in White Adipose Tissue of Obese Women Undergoing Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Three-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract:
Obesity is a complex, multifactorial disease driven by metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis. The pathogenesis of obesity is closely linked to white adipose tissue (WAT) dysfunction, particularly the dysregulation of lipogenic and adipogenic pathways, leading to adipocyte hypertrophy and ectopic fat deposition. Although sleeve gastrectomy is a gold-standard intervention for severe obesity, a subset of patients experiences suboptimal long-term weight loss and cardiometabolic improvements, potentially due to persistent inflammation and metabolic resistance.

The gut-adipose axis has emerged as a critical therapeutic target. Modulation of the gut microbiome through synbiotic supplementation may alleviate metabolic endotoxemia and systemic inflammation, thereby improving energy homeostasis. However, the impact of presurgical synbiotic intervention on adipose tissue remodeling in patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy remains largely unexplored.

This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial (RCT) aims to evaluate the efficacy of synbiotic supplementation in obese women candidates for sleeve gastrectomy. The objective is to investigate the effect of synbiotics on the expression of key lipogenic and adipogenic transcriptional factors (e.g., SREBP-1c, C/EBPα, PPARγ, LXRs) and rate-limiting enzymes (e.g, FAS, ACC) in white adipose tissue.

The study hypothesis is that presurgical synbiotic intervention will modulate adipose tissue function, thereby enhancing postoperative weight loss and improving metabolic profiles. The study aims to provide evidence for a potential therapeutic strategy to optimize clinical outcomes in bariatric patients by targeting the molecular mechanisms underlying adipose tissue expansion.

title: Cytomegalovirus Infection After Transplantation: a Study of New Markers to Optimize the Selection of Antiviral Therapies and Reduce the Risk of Developing Direct and Indirect Infection-related Complications
abstract:
Background and Rationale Cytomegalovirus (CMV) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in recipients of solid organ transplantation (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Current management relies on antiviral prophylaxis or pre-emptive therapy guided primarily by CMV-DNAemia monitoring. However, recently introduced antivirals such as letermovir and maribavir have changed the virological profile of CMV infection, highlighting limitations of DNAemia as a marker of active viral replication and increasing the need for improved resistance monitoring.

Preliminary studies suggest that CMV-RNAemia (UL21.5 mRNA) may be a more accurate marker of active viral replication and may detect viral clearance approximately 7-14 days earlier than CMV-DNAemia. In parallel, Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) may provide superior detection of antiviral resistance mutations, including low-frequency variants that cannot be identified by conventional Sanger sequencing.

Primary Objective To determine whether using CMV-RNAemia to guide discontinuation of antiviral therapy in transplant recipients can reduce treatment duration and drug-related toxicity without increasing the risk of CMV relapse, compared with the current standard based on CMV-DNAemia.

Secondary Objectives

Compare the diagnostic performance of NGS and Sanger sequencing in detecting CMV antiviral resistance mutations.

Estimate the incidence of resistant or refractory CMV infection (R/R-CMV) in transplant recipients.

Identify risk factors associated with the development of R/R-CMV according to transplant type.

Study Design This is a single-center, pragmatic, randomized controlled interventional study conducted at the IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna.

Adult transplant recipients (≥18 years) with CMV infection requiring antiviral therapy will be randomized (1:1) into two groups:

Experimental arm: antiviral therapy discontinued after two consecutive negative CMV-RNAemia results.

Control arm: antiviral therapy discontinued after two consecutive negative CMV-DNAemia results.

Patients will be followed from treatment initiation, with virological monitoring continuing during therapy and follow-up.

Population and Sample Size The study plans to enroll approximately 330 CMV infection episodes, including an estimated 10% drop-out rate, with 150 participants per study arm plus additional cases to compensate for losses.

Endpoints Primary endpoints include:

Time to treatment discontinuation. Time to viral clearance. Incidence and timing of clinically significant CMV relapse. Antiviral drug toxicity.

Secondary endpoints include:

Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive value of NGS versus Sanger sequencing. Incidence of resistant/refractory CMV infection. Identification of clinical and virological risk factors for resistance.

Resistance Analysis In suspected resistant or refractory CMV infections, residual biological samples will undergo NGS analysis targeting CMV genes involved in antiviral resistance (UL97, UL54, UL56, UL89, UL27, UL51). Results will be compared with standard Sanger sequencing to assess earlier detection of resistance mutations and minor viral variants.

Expected Impact The study aims to establish CMV-RNAemia as a clinically useful marker for earlier identification of viral clearance, enabling shorter antiviral treatment and reduced toxicity. It also seeks to validate NGS-based resistance testing as a more sensitive tool for detecting emerging CMV drug resistance, ultimately supporting a more personalized approach to CMV management in transplant recipients and potentially other immunocompromised populations.

Study Duration and Funding The study is expected to last 24 months (18 months recruitment, 4 months follow-up, 2 months analysis) and is funded by the Italian Ministry of Health (Ricerca Corrente 2026, project RC-2026-2802099).

title: Impact of Ozonated Oil on the Ocular Surface and the Expression of Immune and Inflammatory Response Mediators in Middle-Aged Women
abstract:
This study examines the effects of an eye gel containing liposomal ozonated oil in middle-aged women with dry eye disease. Dry eye can cause discomfort, an unstable tear film, and inflammation of the eye surface.

The main questions are whether one week of treatment changes:

Tear film stability and other signs and symptoms of dry eye.

Markers of inflammation in cells collected from the eye surface.

Proteins involved in maintaining connections between eye surface cells.

Women with dry eye use the eye gel for one week and undergo assessments before and after treatment. These assessments include a symptom questionnaire, eye surface examinations, and collection of small samples of cells from the conjunctiva, the thin tissue covering the white of the eye.

A separate group of healthy young women undergoes one assessment without receiving treatment. Their measurements provide reference values for comparison with those of women with dry eye.
description:
This prospective, nonrandomized interventional study combines a before-and-after treatment assessment in women with dry eye disease with a separate healthy reference group.

Women aged 45-65 years with dry eye disease receive a commercially available ophthalmic gel containing liposomal ozonated oil, hydroxyethylcellulose, and poloxamer 407 for one week. Clinical assessments and conjunctival impression cytology are performed at baseline and after treatment. Healthy women aged 18-30 years undergo a single assessment without treatment.

Conjunctival samples are examined using quantitative real-time PCR to assess the expression of inflammatory cytokines, matrix metalloproteinases, and MUC5AC. Immunofluorescence analysis of ZO-1 and E-cadherin is used to examine epithelial junctional organization and cell morphology.

Treatment-associated changes are assessed within the dry eye group. The healthy group provides a biological reference and does not serve as a randomized treatment comparator.

title: A Precision Exercise Approach Using Myostatin/Follistatin Ratio Stratification to Improve Lean Body Mass and Metabolic Health: A 12-Month Randomized Clinical Trial in Obese North Indian Adults
abstract:
This study evaluates whether a 12-month supervised progressive resistance training program improves lean body mass and metabolic health in obese North Indian adults aged 35-60 years. Asian Indians are uniquely predisposed to sarcopenic obesity-the coexistence of excess body fat and reduced muscle mass-which significantly increases the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

Participants will be stratified into High-Ratio and Low-Ratio groups based on their baseline Myostatin/Follistatin (MSTN/FST) ratio, an biological index of muscle catabolism versus growth. Half of the participants in each stratum will undergo a 12-month supervised resistance training program, while the other half will receive standard lifestyle advice. The primary goal is to determine whether baseline MSTN/FST ratio predicts the extent of muscle mass gain and whether reducing this ratio mediates improvements in insulin resistance and systemic inflammation.
description:
Background \& Scientific Rationale: Sarcopenic obesity is a major driver of cardiometabolic risk in Asian Indians due to low baseline lean mass combined with high visceral adiposity. Myostatin (MSTN) acts as a primary negative regulator of muscle growth, whereas follistatin (FST) acts as its circulating antagonist. Previous genetic research demonstrates that gain-of-function Myostatin gene variants are strongly associated with lower lean body mass and increased adiposity in North Indians. This trial prospectively tests whether the serum MSTN/FST ratio functions as a precision biomarker to stratify exercise response and guide targeted exercise interventions.

Study Objectives:

Determine the efficacy of a 12-month supervised resistance training program on total lean body mass (LBM) and physical performance compared to lifestyle control, testing for treatment interaction across baseline MSTN/FST strata.

Characterize the molecular adaptations of the myostatin axis by measuring serum myostatin, follistatin, MSTN/FST ratio, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) MSTN mRNA expression at baseline and 12 months.

Assess whether reductions in the MSTN/FST ratio mediate improvements in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), systemic inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF-α, hsCRP), and muscle quality.

Trial Design \& Interventions: A single-center, ratio-stratified, 1:1 parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial of 200 obese North Indian adults.

Resistance Training Arm (n=100): 3 supervised sessions per week (60 minutes per session) at 70-80% 1-repetition maximum (1RM) using progressive resistance overload reassessed every 8 weeks.

Control Arm (n=100): Standard individualized dietary and physical activity advice per national guidelines without supervised exercise sessions.

Outcome Assessments: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) for total LBM, appendicular lean mass, and body fat percentage; handgrip dynamometry and 1RM testing for strength; quantitative ELISA for serum biomarkers; real-time qRT-PCR (2-ΔΔCt method) for PBMC MSTN mRNA expression; and standardized biochemical panels for glycemic and inflammatory profiles.

title: Immunogenicity of the CpG 1018-Adjuvanted CORBEVAX COVID-19 Vaccine in Adults With and Without Helminth Infection (Schistosoma Mansoni or Hookworm) in Ethiopia
abstract: Helminth infections affect over 1.5 billion people and weaken the response to vaccination. CORBEVAX contains the TLR9-activating adjuvant CpG 1018, which may overcome this. This trial measures the immunogenicity of CORBEVAX in adults with and without Schistosoma mansoni or hookworm infection in Ethiopia. The primary measure is spike-specific serum IgG at Day 42; antibody subclass, T-cell, neutralisation and regulatory T-cell responses are measured as secondary outcomes up to Day 90. This is the first of two planned cohorts under a shared protocol; a second cohort receiving an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine at the same sites is planned subject to vaccine availability and will be registered separately.
description:
Adults aged 18 years or older living in helminth -endemic (Schistosoma mansoni and hookworm ) areas of Ethiopia (Bahir Dar and Arba Minch) are recruited by community-based mobilisation, screened by parasitological examination (direct wet mount and Kato-Katz) and classified as helminth-infected or uninfected before enrolment. The study has a single arm: every participant receives CORBEVAX intramuscularly (0.5 ml undiluted) at Day 0 with a homologous booster at Day 28, and the helminth-infected and uninfected groups differ by baseline exposure rather than by assigned intervention. Serum is collected at Day 0, Day 42 and Day 90, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) are isolated at Day 0 and Day 42, so that all cell-based outcomes have a pre-vaccination baseline. Infected participants receive anthelminthic treatment after the Day 42 blood draw. Immunological assays are run at Aarhus University, with neutralizing antibody testing at Biological E, India.

This study is the first of two sequential cohorts conducted under a shared protocol, at the same study sites, with the same field teams, eligibility criteria, visit schedule, outcome measures and laboratory assays. A second cohort, in which participants will receive an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine (BNT162b2, or mRNA-1273 if BNT162b2 cannot be obtained), is planned to begin enrolment approximately one month after the last participant is enrolled in the present cohort, subject to vaccine availability, and will be registered as a separate record carrying the same protocol identifier.

Participants are not allocated to a vaccine platform: the vaccine a participant receives is determined by which cohort is enrolling at the time. Because each cohort contains its own contemporaneous helminth-uninfected comparison group, a prespecified secondary analysis will compare the infected-versus-uninfected response ratio between the two cohorts (a difference-in-differences comparison across vaccine platforms) rather than comparing vaccine groups directly. Serum and PBMC samples from both cohorts will be stored and assayed together in a single batch with shared reference standards and bridging controls, and baseline anti-nucleocapsid serology will be measured in both cohorts to document comparability of prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Antigen, dose and formulation differ between the two vaccine platforms, so any between-cohort difference cannot be attributed to adjuvants alone.

A single primary outcome is specified: spike-specific serum IgG concentration at Day 42. Serum is obtained from every participant at every visit and the assay is performed in-house, so this measure is the one least exposed to sample or logistical failure. All remaining immunological read-outs are secondary. Analyses that require viable PBMC will be performed in every participant from whom cells of adequate viability are recovered; if adequate cells are not recovered in a sufficient proportion of participants, those analyses will be reported as exploratory rather than omitted. Serum, PBMC and faecal aliquots are biobanked under the storage consent, so any assay deferred for sample or budget reasons can be completed later rather than lost.

outcomes.description: Number of helminth eggs per gram of stool (EPG), measured by Kato-Katz thick smear microscopy. EPG is the mean egg count from two thick smears prepared from a single stool sample, multiplied by 24 (41.7 mg template). Reported separately for Schistosoma mansoni and hookworm as the geometric mean EPG with 95% confidence interval.

outcomes.measure: Percentage of participants with parasitological clearance
outcomes.description: Percentage of participants with EPG = 0 on Kato-Katz microscopy at Day 90 among participants with EPG \> 0 at baseline, assessed separately for Schistosoma mansoni and hookworm, following anthelmintic treatment given after Day 42. Newly acquired infection (EPG \> 0 at Day 90 among participants with EPG = 0 at baseline) will be addressed in a prespecified sensitivity analysis.

outcomes.measure: Correlation between baseline helminth egg count and Day 42 anti-spike IgG concentration
outcomes.description: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rho) between two measures in the same participants: (1) baseline EPG, measured by Kato-Katz thick smear at Day 0 (eggs per gram of stool); and (2) serum anti-spike IgG concentration at Day 42, measured by in-house ELISA (AU/mL). Calculated separately for Schistosoma mansoni and hookworm. Reported with 95% confidence interval.

outcomes.measure: Correlation between baseline gut microbiota alpha diversity and Day 42 serum anti-spike IgG concentration
outcomes.description: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rho) between two measures in the same participants: (1) baseline faecal bacterial alpha diversity, expressed as the Shannon index (unitless), calculated from 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (V3-V4 region) of a single stool sample collected at Day 0; and (2) serum anti-spike IgG concentration at Day 42, measured by in-house ELISA and expressed in arbitrary units per mL (AU/mL). Reported with 95% confidence interval.

outcomes.measure: Number and percentage of participants with solicited and unsolicited adverse events after vaccination
outcomes.description: Number and percentage of participants reporting at least one solicited local or systemic adverse event (injection-site pain, redness or swelling, fatigue, headache, fever, myalgia) or any unsolicited adverse event, including serious adverse events, after each vaccine dose.

title: RNA PRIME - RNA Lipid Particles Targeting Pediatric Recurrent Intracranial Malignancies and Other systEmic Solid Tumors
abstract:
The Investigators have demonstrated in preclinical studies that RNA liposomes activate APCs, induce antigen-specific T cell immunity, and can supplant DCs in a cell therapy model for HGG and have shown feasibility and activity of this approach in preclinical models and in canine patients with a spontaneous malignant glioma. In one arm of this study, we will investigate the safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccines in pediatric patients with recurrent pHGG.

The investigators have also shown that intravenous administration of tumor mRNA loaded lipid particles (LPs) localizes primarily to lung, transfect antigen presenting cells (APCs) and lead to an activated T cell response for induction of anti-tumor immunity. In contrast to other formulations, RNA-LPs recruit multiple arms of the immune system (i.e. innate/adaptive), and remodel the systemic/intratumoral immune milieu, which remain potent barriers for vaccine, cellular, and checkpoint inhibiting immunotherapies. After only a single RNA-LP vaccine, the bulk of systemic and intratumoral dendritic cells (DCs) in mice display an activated phenotype; these activated DCs (harvested from tumors) expand antigen specific T cell immunity. In immunologically resistant pulmonary osteosacroma murine tumor models (i.e. K7M2), RNA-LPs induce robust anti-tumor efficacy in settings where immune checkpoint inhibitors (i.e. anti-PD-L1 therapy) do not confer therapeutic benefit. The investigators have already demonstrated safety of RNA-LPs in acute/chronic murine toxicity studies, and in client-owned canine trial.

In this study, we will investigate the manufacturing feasibility, safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccine in patients with recurrent pulmonary or unresectable osteosarcoma and recurrent pHGG.
description:
For recurrent pHGG there will be two non-randomized arms assigned at the discretion of the patient and treatment team:

* Arm 1-A single neoadjuvant pp65 RNA-LP (DP1) will be administered prior to surgical resection/biopsy, and then two adjuvant DP1.
* Arm 2-Surgical resection/biopsy will occur first and all three DP1 will be administered in the adjuvant setting

The Phase I dose-escalation study for recurrent/progressive pHGG cohort will be performed in 18 subjects using a 3+3 design. Both recurrent pHGG trial arms will be enrolled together as a single cohort for safety.
